solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In Australia a capital idea and deal that's extraordinary

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praises a brilliant scheme and a remarkable bargain struck Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's extraordinary' rearranges IDEA and DEAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia, so it is a capital city found in Australia.

clue.text: Knowing military music hasn't started

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for the music is missing, as if it never began

parts.note: a march is music for soldiers to step to

explanation.surface: A worldly person dismisses the sound of a military band before it begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means sly, mischievous and knowing, as in an arch look.

clue.text: Model partner once generous

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
a generous helping is an ample one

explanation.surface: A fashion model's former partner was free-handed with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to follow is a pattern or exemplar, something worth copying.

clue.text: Take illegally? Right

definitions.meaning: to seize something for oneself without permission, as funds are misused
fitting or suitable for the occasion

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether stealing is acceptable and is answered with a reassuring yes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to take for one's own use without right; as an adjective it means suitable or proper.

clue.text: Nothing that is dear

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off something trivial with a fond word of address.
explanation.walkthrough: A DUCK is a cricketer's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckie is an informal British term of endearment, like darling or love.

clue.text: Dessert made by wife with it

parts.note: someone with it is fashionable, or hip

explanation.surface: A trendy wife has made the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip is a light pudding of beaten cream or egg whites, often with fruit.

clue.text: Dye hard girl picked up

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, as by a microphone, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils; Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tough girl who coloured her hair was collected by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' says H plus ANNA, said aloud, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant-based colouring used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Nasty MEP fiddled allowances

indicators.note: fiddled figures have been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpleasant Member of the European Parliament fiddled his expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' rearranges NASTY MEP; an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are sums paid out to someone, so they are payments.

clue.text: Fellow boxing minute title-holder

indicators.note: boxing something encloses it, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a chap is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A man boxes for a minute against the reigning champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is short for champion, the holder of a sporting title.

clue.text: Effectiveness of company shown by data extremely clearly

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A firm's performance is plainly demonstrated by its figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogency is the forcefulness of an argument, its power to persuade.

clue.text: Market trader perhaps is inexperienced and rather vulgar, we hear

parts.note: a green recruit is inexperienced

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: grosser means more coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A street seller is said to be naive and somewhat crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of fruit and vegetables may well run a market stall, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Feel airport needs changing to grow rapidly (ll)

indicators.note: letters that need changing are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone senses that an airport must change in order to expand quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply or spread quickly in number.

clue.text: Curate finally happy in restored church festival

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken
something restored is rebuilt, so these letters are reworked into new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is finally contented in a church that has been renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges HAPPY IN to make PIPHANY, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Epiphany, on 6 January, is the Christian feast marking the Magi's visit.

clue.text: US author to judge verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
to try a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: An American writer is called on to assess some lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing, the same thing as poems collectively.

clue.text: Complete current book and part of play

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: A finished up-to-date volume contains a section of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, nothing missing.

clue.text: Cross written at bottom of a contract

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece is written beneath the first

parts.note: to bridge a gap is to cross it

explanation.surface: An angry signature is scrawled at the foot of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun, a legal agreement, but it is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, making it shrink.

clue.text: Stick lands regularly at this spot

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word picks it at regular intervals

parts.note: here means at this place

explanation.surface: A walking stick is regularly put down at this very place.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached, as glue does.

clue.text: Boy accompanying queen twice is a Casanova

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
and joins one thing to another, as company does

indicators.note: the queen's abbreviation appears two times in a row

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of a queen

explanation.surface: A lad seen escorting royalty repeatedly is a notorious lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was a famous seducer, so his name stands for any womaniser.

clue.text: Playwright identified by some lines bitterly upset

indicators.note: in a down answer something upset is turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
some of the words means a run of letters taken from within them

explanation.surface: A dramatist recognised by a few harsh lines is deeply upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes NESBI from inside 'lines bitterly'; 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House.

clue.text: Garden party making fortune reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: fate is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: An outdoor party is said to have made someone's fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event, often held in a garden.

clue.text: Famous authoress with no name on grave

indicators.note: having no part of a word means that part is taken out

parts.note: Jane Austen is the celebrated English novelist
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A well-known novelist lies in an unmarked grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and grave both mean severe and serious in manner.

clue.text: Group of revolutionary activists with duke in charge

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: something in your care is in your charge

explanation.surface: A band of militants has a nobleman leading them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained activists in a political movement.

clue.text: American is a jerk

definitions.meaning: an informal term for someone from the United States
a sudden sharp pull or tug

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a person from the US is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a US citizen, and also a sudden hard pull on something.

clue.text: Traveller always recalled carrying one spare

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, travels for work

indicators.note: one word carries the other inside it
something called back runs in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A salesman forever remembered carrying a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts I into EVER to give EVEIR; 'recalled' turns that round to RIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprieve someone is to spare them a punishment, especially execution.
